issue.title: `'?$'`, which is not a valid integer literal, hence the `ValueError`., kills the app

steps: Find the installed gptme package's tools/shell.py file (for example with `python -c "import gptme.tools.shell as s; print(s.__file__)"`).
Run the shell command `head -n 1000 <that path>` to show its contents.
expected: The file's first 1000 lines are shown as normal shell output and the session continues.
defect: Printing shell.py's own source (which contains the `echo ReturnCode:$?` marker text) makes the return-code parser raise `ValueError: invalid literal for int() ... '$?'`, which kills the app.
Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/commit/becab4d69a85f2c769f610f6200de44c7fabdcaf. The 2023 shell tool detected the end of a command by scanning stdout for a line containing `ReturnCode:<n> <delimiter>` and converting the token after `ReturnCode:` with int(). When the command's own output is gptme's shell.py source, the literal text `echo ReturnCode:$? ...` matches first, int('$?') raises ValueError, and because execute_msg did not catch tool exceptions the exception propagated through the chat loop and terminated gptme. Commit becab4d ('fix: catch exceptions from tools and propagate as messages', linked from the issue page) wraps execute_codeblock in try/except and yields a system message instead of crashing; the return-code parsing was later rewritten to match only `ReturnCode:(\d+)` together with the delimiter (PR #335) and the current code strips a per-session marker. The crash fix first ships in v0.11.1; the pinned revision contains both changes.
